- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp negative swings, model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility clustering.
- When true outcome shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior), model frequently fails to catch it; increase sensitivity to recent highs and sentiment momentum.
- If model forecast is flat or slowly rising while true price rises sharply, model underestimates momentum; adjust for sentiment-driven acceleration.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true price reverses or drops, model may be ignoring mean reversion; apply early correction if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral/bearish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; reduce persistence of recent trend in forecast if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -1.00, -0.50), model tends to underestimate subsequent drop; add downward bias or lagged sentiment multiplier.
